market_demand_anchors.evidence: The Chao Phraya Express Boat river boats carry an average of about 40,000 passengers per day across a ~21 km system.

market_demand_anchors.source: Wikipedia / Thai Smile Boat (ex-MINE Smart Ferry)
market_demand_anchors.evidence: Thai Smile Boat (formerly MINE Smart Ferry): electric catamaran fleet of 35 vessels, 22 piers, 3 lines (City/Metro/Urban), hub Sathorn Pier; vessels 150-250 pax; began 2020.

corridors.corridor: Chao Phraya river spine: Sathorn (CEN) <-> ICONSIAM (N2/1) <-> Phra Arthit (N13) corridor
corridors.vessel_gate: <=70nm -> N30 Pioneer II / N35 Shuttle (dense urban legs)
corridors.premium_ceiling_note: Private long-tail / dinner-cruise charters list THB 1,500-15,000; Navier premium positioning sits above the THB 150 tourist day-pass, below charter.

demand_anchors.evidence: ~40,000 passengers/day system-wide; Sathorn is the central interchange (BTS Saphan Taksin).
Tourist boats depart every 30 min from 11 piers incl. Sathorn, ICONSIAM, Ratchawongse, Yodpiman.

inputs.share_basis: Share of the 40k/day on the central Sathorn-ICONSIAM-Phra Arthit tourist/commuter spine (vs outer commuter piers). LABELLED ASSUMPTION.
inputs.premium_share_basis: Share willing to pay a premium electric-foil fare above the THB 10-30 commuter floor (hotel guests, ICONSIAM/riverside, airport-rail interchange). Labelled assumption - low because this is a deeply price-anchored commuter market.

derived_demand_record.calc: 40,000/day * 360 = 14.4M system pax/yr. Central tourist corridor = 14.4M * 0.30 = 4.32M/yr. Premium-eligible = 4.32M * 0.08 = ~345,600 premium one-way trips/yr.
derived_demand_record.fare_basis: THB 150 tourist day-pass as the premium-tier reference (NOT the THB 10 commuter floor); a foiling premium transfer is positioned at the tourist/hotel tier.
